deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous and next pages): Grothendieck is axiomatising a 'tame' class F of subsets of a space X. F_0 is the set of closed members of F. F appears to be the Boolean algebra generated by F_0, so its elements are finite unions of locally closed sets B−C with B, C in F_0.

The axioms appear to be:
- α, β (a, b): lattice and Boolean closure conditions not involving the topology.
- γ (c): the closure of a member of F lies in F_0.
- δ (d): no infinite descending chain A_1 ⊃ A_2 ⊃ … in F with each A_{n+1} rare in A_n. This is a finite-dimension or Noetherian-type condition.

On the previous page he observed that closure of members of F is computable from F_0 alone. So 'rare' and δ can be stated intrinsically in F_0.

This page answers his question: given an abstract family F_0 of subsets of a set X, when is there a topology on X for which F_0 satisfies α, β, γ (and δ)? Answer: α, β plus
- γ') for all A, B in F_0 there is a smallest element of F_0 containing A∩∁B.

In modern terms: there is a least C in F_0 with A ⊂ B∪C, i.e. a co-Heyting (Brouwerian) subtraction A∸B on the lattice F_0, realised by closure of the set difference.

Sufficiency: let T be the topology whose closed sets are arbitrary intersections of elements of F_0. These are stable under finite unions by distributivity, (∩A_i)∪(∩B_j) = ∩(A_i∪B_j), given that F_0 is stable under finite unions.
- The T-closure of A−B is the intersection of the elements of F_0 containing it, which by γ') is the smallest such element. So γ holds.
- Since closures of finite unions are unions of closures, γ for all of F follows.
- T is the coarsest admissible topology, since F_0 must consist of closed sets.
- T is characterised by condition (b): F_0 is a base of closed sets. Equivalently, every open set is a union of open members of F, or every point has a fundamental system of neighbourhoods in F.

NB on this page: if F satisfies a)–d) and A ∈ F, then the boundary ∂A = Ā − Å is rare (nowhere dense) in X. Sketch: let U be the interior of ∂A. U is in F, since interiors of members of F are complements of closures of members of F. Restricting the structure to U preserves a)–d). One is reduced to showing that if Ā = X and Å = ∅ then X = ∅. He stops there with 'X = ∂A …'.

A struck vertical marginal note about connected components of locally closed members of F prepares condition f) on the next page: finitely many components, each lying in F.
errors: γ') is stated loosely as 'the set of elements of F_0 containing A∩∁B is in F_0'. What is meant is that its intersection (the least element) belongs to F_0; the parenthesis gives the correct reading.

The NB's proof is left unfinished. However, the claim needs neither δ nor any tameness. In any topological space ∂(B∩O) ⊂ ∂B ∪ ∂O, ∂(A∪A') ⊂ ∂A ∪ ∂A', boundaries of open and of closed sets are nowhere dense, and finite unions of nowhere dense sets are nowhere dense. So the boundary of any finite union of locally closed sets is nowhere dense. The reduction via restriction to U is correct but heavier than necessary.
Minimality of T 'among the topologies considered': strictly, he should note that for a finer topology the closures must still be the F_0-least elements for γ to hold. This is implicit, not argued.

ideas.what: Intrinsic characterisation: the closure of A−B (A, B closed tame sets) is the least element of F_0 containing it, so tameness data can be given by a lattice F_0 of closed sets without a prior topology.
ideas.modern_name: co-Heyting (Brouwerian) algebra of closed definable/constructible sets; closure algebra in the sense of McKinsey–Tarski
ideas.usually_credited_to: McKinsey–Tarski (closure algebras, 1944; Brouwerian algebras, 1946); for definable closed sets, the o-minimal and semialgebraic literature (van den Dries, Pillay, Coste–Roy, Delfs–Knebusch)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for an axiomatic tame topology; no such axioms are given there

ideas.what: Coarsest topology generated by F_0 as a base of closed sets; F_0 being a base of closed sets is equivalent to points having fundamental systems of tame neighbourhoods.
ideas.modern_name: topology generated by a lattice of closed sets; cf. the restricted/generalized topology of Delfs–Knebusch locally semialgebraic spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard general topology; Delfs–Knebusch (1985) for semialgebraic generalized topologies

ideas.what: The boundary of a tame set is nowhere dense.
ideas.modern_name: boundary of a constructible / definable set is nowhere dense (dim ∂A < dim A in o-minimal geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; the dimension version is due to van den Dries / Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn

ideas.what: Stating 'rare' and a descending-chain condition (δ) purely in terms of the lattice F_0, as an abstract dimension axiom.
ideas.modern_name: finite Krull dimension / finite depth of a (co-)Heyting algebra; dimension axioms for o-minimal or geometric structures
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (o-minimal dimension theory); Bezhanishvili et al. (Krull dimension of Heyting algebras)

missed.claim: Condition γ') is exactly the requirement that the lattice F_0 of closed tame sets be a co-Heyting algebra whose subtraction is closure of set difference. Combined with the previous page's intrinsic notion of 'F_0-rare' (A_n ∸ A_{n+1} = A_n) and axiom δ, this gives an algebraic, point-free axiomatisation of tame topology: a co-Heyting algebra of finite 'rare-chain' dimension, plus later the connectedness axiom f). This links Grothendieck's tame-topology programme to Lawvere's co-Heyting boundary calculus (∂A = A ∧ ¬A) and to Krull dimension of Heyting algebras. To my knowledge that link is not made explicitly in the o-minimal literature.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a point-free or topos-theoretic formulation of 'tame topology' via co-Heyting algebras with dimension. That is close to how one would approach Grothendieck's Esquisse demand intrinsically, and it complements the model-theoretic o-minimal framework.

missed.claim: A 1974 attempt at an axiomatic tame topology in terms of a family F_0 of closed sets, independent of any ambient topology, ten years before the Esquisse and before o-minimality (1984–86). It is historically noteworthy, though the content on this page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is elementary: a closure condition, the generated topology, and a nowhere-density claim whose proof stops unfinished and which in fact holds in any space. The interest is historical, an early (1974) lattice-theoretic axiomatisation of tame topology, and the implicit co-Heyting structure, which is a modest unremarked connection.
transcription_corrections: 'r')' is most likely 'γ')', the modified axiom γ.
'des ensembles quelconques d'éléments de F_0' should read 'des intersections quelconques d'éléments de F_0' (closed sets of T are arbitrary intersections).
'Ceci suffisait [?], car on peut déf. la top. T' is plausibly 'Ceci suffit, car on peut prendre la top. T'.
'les Ȧ sont [?] dans X' should read 'les Ȧ sont rares dans X' (boundary nowhere dense).
'(ou de voisinages ouverts ∋ F)' should read '(ou de voisinages ouverts ∈ F)'.
'nous induisons sur U' is plausibly 'nous induisons sur U', i.e. restrict the structure to U; the reading is uncertain but the meaning is clear.
In the last line, 'prouvons que si Ā=X, Å=∅ alors X=∅' has an interlinear addition reading roughly 'Å ∋ … i.e. X = Ȧ'; the intended reduction is that the open set U equals its own boundary part.
